newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady, hovers at $120-$122/t.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady, hovers at $120-$122/t.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to be quoted around Wednesday's levels, traders said.
They said 180-cst cargoes for end October/early November loading were bid/asked at $120/$121 per tonne on Wednesday.
They said there is no lack of supplies in the market to meet demand and physical prices were supported by firm sentiment.
A western trader said he would place an offer for late October/November barrels at $122 per tonne.
"Market prices are currently driven more by strong sentiment caused by firm crude prices," said the trader.
Pockets of demand were seen from Indonesia, Vietnam and China but these are not strong enough to support prices, said another trader.
Traders said most Chinese demand were covered out of South Korea.
October paper swaps remained steady at $121/$122.
